T1.prompt:
Founders of registered channels keep asking for a way to welcome people. Please let a channel's founder set a greeting that ChanServ gives everyone who joins.

- `/msg ChanServ ENTRYMSG #channel <text>` sets it, and `/msg ChanServ ENTRYMSG #channel` on its own removes it. ChanServ confirms either way.
- Only the founder can change it, and network staff (opers with the chanreg capability).
- Standing rule for ChanServ from now on: anything it says to people that nobody asked for (as opposed to a reply to a command) goes out as a NOTICE, and the line starts with the channel's name in square brackets, spelled the way the channel was registered, like `[#Lobby] Welcome!`. I want every unprompted message to look like that, not only this one.
- 200 characters at most; refuse anything longer rather than cutting it. Our users write in many languages.
- It has to survive a server restart.

One more thing, for later rather than for this. It's a rule for any ChanServ command we make staff-only: every time one gets used, the other operators have to be told, with a server notice on the channels mask that reads exactly `STAFF <account> <COMMAND> <#channel>`, the command in capitals and the channel as registered.

Keep the project's existing behaviour and checks working.

T2.prompt:
Network staff want to keep private notes on channels: who complained, what was agreed with the founder. Please add a ChanServ NOTE command.

- `NOTE #channel ADD <text>`, `NOTE #channel LIST`, `NOTE #channel DEL <number>`.
- Only the channel's founder and network staff (opers with the chanreg capability) may use it. To anyone else ChanServ must give exactly the same answer whether or not the channel has notes: it must not be possible to find out that notes exist.
- LIST shows the newest note first, one line each: `#<number> <date and time> UTC <account>: <text>`, for example `#2 2026-11-17 09:30 UTC alice: agreed to unban bob`. The staff dashboard reads these lines, so keep exactly that format. (Everything else new that ChanServ shows with a date and time is going to be RFC 3339 in UTC, like `2026-11-17T09:30:00Z`. Notes are the one exception.)
- Showing the author's account is fine here because only staff and founders read notes. (By the way, whenever we tell a founder about something staff did, we only ever say `network staff`, never which of us. They get prickly otherwise.)
- A note keeps its number: deleting #2 leaves #1 and #3 as they are.
- A channel can hold 10 notes; refuse an 11th.
- Notes survive a server restart.

Keep the project's existing behaviour and checks working.
